minutes.headline: Select Board heard DPW staffing and pay pleas, ratified a DPW hire, and planned a December workshop and policy reviews.
minutes.summary: Public comment dominated the meeting. The town manager corrected cemetery labor hours and described meeting DPW staff, and residents, a former selectman, and the firefighters' union president spoke about low pay, turnover and morale. The board ratified a DPW driver/laborer appointment, issued a commendation for a local farm owner, and discussed bylaw chapters and the remote participation policy for December, along with a workshop on making Lunenburg a place to live, work and volunteer.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the town manager and described low morale, turnover and pay at the DPW; objected to the chair's prior remarks about cemetery hours; asked for a pay comparison and consultation with supervisors on job classification.
Said last week's comments about cemetery staffing were ill-timed and unfair; praised the cemetery's upkeep.
Praised the cemetery worker and asked for closed captioning on the broadcast.
Praised the DPW and thanked the town manager; asked for no more criticism.
Thanked the town manager; said public safety departments are also stretched, salaries slip behind neighboring towns, and department heads lack succession plans.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said funding for wages and future costs of insufficient staffing is the top issue to address.
The town manager corrected the estimate of seasonal cemetery hours and gave the actual hours worked.
A speaker recalled the chair questioning paying for far more hours than the work done.
A member recalled questioning an earlier warrant article request and noted the corrected hours differ greatly from the first figure.
The town received a technical assistance award for the property project, less than the original request, so the scope will be narrowed.
A payroll deduction warrant and an accounts payable warrant were read.
Capital planning received many department requests totalling over a stated amount.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to cancel the November 21 meeting and reschedule it for November 28, when boards will give annual reports.
Review of bylaw chapter five deferred to December to allow the town manager and counsel to review.
Remote participation policy (chapter 305) to be discussed at the first December meeting; the town manager will provide current state law for comparison.
Review of town-owned properties in the WHM area postponed to another time.
Workshop on what makes Lunenburg a great place to live, work and volunteer to be held at the second December meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board ratified the town manager's appointment of a DPW driver/laborer by roll call, all members voting aye as heard.
Public comment ran long: residents, a former selectman and the firefighters' union president spoke about DPW pay, turnover and morale.
The town manager said DPW wages and the future cost of insufficient staffing are the top issue, and corrected the seasonal cemetery hours given earlier.
The board deferred the bylaw chapter review and the remote participation policy to December, and set a workshop on living, working and volunteering in Lunenburg for the second December meeting.
The board moved the November 21 meeting to November 28, when boards give annual reports, and issued a commendation to a local farm owner by roll call.

why_it_matters: DPW pay and staffing were raised as the main budget pressure, and wage decisions there flow into the town's operating budget and the warrant articles residents vote on at town meeting.
Residents who want to weigh in on the remote participation policy or on town priorities have December meetings to do it at, since both items were set for then.
